headline: A scientist at the Israeli company Quantum X Labs argues that quantum sensors could keep vehicles and aircraft on course when GPS is blocked or faked.
score_reason: Pool score 4 lowered by 1 because it is one company scientist's argument with lab prototypes only, no new result and no figures.
importance_line: Makers of self-driving cars, aircraft and defence systems that rely on GPS are the people this idea is aimed at, but it is one company's view, its devices exist only as laboratory prototypes, and the piece gives no test results or launch dates.
summary: The Next Web publishes the argument of Nir Sharon, chief quantum technology scientist at Quantum X Labs and a Tel Aviv University professor, that quantum gyroscopes and very precise small clocks could reduce the small errors that build up when a machine works out its position from its own movement, so it can keep navigating without GPS. He says the company's devices are lab prototypes and that turning them into products is now mainly an engineering job.
notes: Company-view piece; the claims are Quantum X Labs' own.
